clue.text: It may be cut and pickled

definitions.text: It may be cut and pickled

parts.words: It may be cut and pickled
parts.note: one cuts a playful leap, and the little flower bud of a Mediterranean shrub is preserved in brine

explanation.surface: Something from the deli counter that gets sliced and preserved in vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gherkin or cheese; in fact 'cut' belongs to the idiom of cutting a frisky jump, while the pickled sense is the bud used in tartare sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a frolicsome skip is something you cut, and the bush's buds are sold pickled.

clue.text: Not a charge for wardrobe equipment

indicators.note: for here is the weak signal that the letters of the preceding words are to be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A service offered free of charge for fitting out a wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Not a charge' are rearranged; there is no strong anagram signal, so 'for' must be read as 'converted into'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger for coats is a standard fitting hung on the rail inside a clothes cupboard.

clue.text: Fruit no good for pudding

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
duff is British slang for useless or no good

explanation.surface: Fruit that has gone off, unsuitable for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFF is British slang for worthless; a plum duff is a boiled suet pudding with raisins.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum duff is a traditional steamed suet dessert studded with dried fruit.

clue.text: Russian family rule that came to an end in a revolutionary way

definitions.text: Russian family rule that came to an end in a revolutionary way

parts.words: Russian family rule that came to an end in a revolutionary way
parts.note: describes the tsarist dynasty whose reign was ended by the 1917 revolution

explanation.surface: A Russian dynasty's reign was ended by revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The last ruling house of the tsars was overthrown in the revolution of 1917.

clue.text: He wrote comedies many never go out to see

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so a large number

indicators.note: out signals the letters of these words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A playwright whose comedies are so dull that many people refuse ever to attend them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes ONGREVE from the letters of 'never go'; 'to see' is a link. William Congreve wrote Restoration comedies such as The Way of the World.
explanation.definitionFit: William Congreve was the Restoration dramatist behind The Way of the World and Love for Love.

clue.text: New cost of baby beds

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters of the next word are remade in another order

explanation.surface: The price of new cribs for infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges 'cost'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cots are small beds with high sides for infants.

clue.text: Tax-protester who presented her buff form

definitions.text: Tax-protester who presented her buff form

parts.words: Tax-protester who presented her buff form
parts.note: reads like someone filing a tax form, but recalls the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry

explanation.surface: A woman objecting to tax sends in her yellowish return.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the Saxon noblewoman rode naked (in the buff) through Coventry to make her husband lift a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva is the legendary Coventry rider who went naked in protest at her husband's taxes.

clue.text: Outpace former top tennis player, we hear

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: we hear signals that the following letters are the spoken sound of a word

parts.note: a seed is a highly ranked tennis player

explanation.surface: Getting ahead of a former leading tennis champion, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means SEED is spelt by its sound as CEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond or surpass, like going faster than a rival.

clue.text: Issue of US magazine turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Time is an American news magazine

explanation.surface: An edition of an American magazine has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses TIME in this down clue. 'Issue' looks like a magazine edition but is the verb, send out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or discharge, as to issue a sound or light.

clue.text: Only men go in at such a meeting

indicators.note: go in tells us the following pieces are placed inside the word at

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gathering where only men are admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only' reads as restricting who attends, but it is the synonym 'but', as in 'but a child'; 'go in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is a place where two structures touch or join, a meeting of parts.

clue.text: Small sum of money sent round as deposit

indicators.note: round means the word sent is wrapped around the coin

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin, a small sum

explanation.surface: A little cash is posted off to secure something, as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the word 'sent' around the coin. 'deposit' looks like a down payment, but it is the silt sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles and is laid down, a geological deposit.

clue.text: There's a regular stream at day's end

parts.note: even means steady or uniform, so regular
a tide is a flowing current of water

explanation.surface: A steady flow of water that runs at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: He'd toss a coin, seeking pleasure

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: to toss something is to throw it about, so the letters of coin are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man flips a coin to decide on his next indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toss' looks like the coin flip of the surface, but it is the anagram signal working on 'coin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonic describes things relating to or pursuing enjoyment, as in hedonism.

clue.text: Many woken when people had a drunken party

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
aroused means woken from sleep

explanation.surface: Lots of people were woken by a noisy drunken party nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily with others.

clue.text: Rag-time band leader was great

definitions.meaning: Irving Berlin's song ... Ragtime Band names its bandleader
the Macedonian king is known to history as 'the Great'

explanation.surface: A ragtime bandleader who was a terrific performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin's song is about Alexander's Ragtime Band, and the conqueror of Persia was Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Limited form of credit provided after period of unemployment

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged credit behind the rest period

parts.note: a rest is a spell without work

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so the letters of credit are reshaped

explanation.surface: Restricted credit is offered once a jobless spell has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges 'credit', placed 'after' the rest; 'provided' is a link. Actors say they are 'resting' when out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricted means kept within bounds or confined.

clue.text: Tribute provided by the gallery for inborn talent?

parts.note: a gift is an offering made in tribute
from means coming from a source, so provided by
taken as written
the gods is a theatre's highest gallery

explanation.surface: A present from the theatre audience in the upper circle as a reward for natural talent.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the cheap top gallery is nicknamed 'the gods'.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is called a godsend or heaven-sent present, something innate rather than learned.

clue.text: Insect with wings of short span

definitions.text: Insect with wings of short span

parts.words: Insect with wings of short span
parts.note: suggests a bug with stubby wings, but recalls the mayfly genus and things that last a very short time

explanation.surface: A bug whose wingspan is small.
explanation.walkthrough: Ephemera is the genus name of mayflies, which live only a day; 'short span' points to lifespan, not wingspan.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayflies, famous for living only a day, belong to a genus named for brevity, and short-lived things share the name.

clue.text: I plan too haphazardly but it's a matter of choice

indicators.note: haphazardly means without order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: My planning is random, but that's up to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazardly' rearranges the letters of 'I plan too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to the individual to decide, not compulsory.

clue.text: Took part in a dramatic trial

definitions.text: Took part in a dramatic trial

parts.words: Took part in a dramatic trial
parts.note: reads like being a witness in a sensational court case, but means practising a role in a run-through before the play opens

explanation.surface: Someone appeared in a sensational court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise their parts in a trial run of the play before opening night.

clue.text: Cast ashore? That's rough

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A castaway washed up on the beach finds it a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges 'ashore'. 'rough' refers to the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarse voice is harsh and grating, rough-sounding.

clue.text: A news broadcast with right to reply

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of news are scattered

explanation.surface: A news bulletin that comes with the right to respond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles 'news' into NSWE, between A and R; 'with' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a response given to a question or remark.

clue.text: Professors discharged-ie retired and retaining worth

indicators.note: retaining means holding the other piece within it
retired means drawn back, so the letters ie run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
merit means worth or value

explanation.surface: Discharged professors, that is retired ones, keep their value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns 'ie' backwards and 'retaining' holds the worth inside. 'discharged' completes the definition: emeriti are professors who have left active service.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus professors are those who have retired but keep their title honorifically.

clue.text: They're often found in a lather

definitions.text: They're often found in a lather

parts.words: They're often found in a lather
parts.note: being in a lather suggests agitated people, but foam on soapy water is literally a lather

explanation.surface: People who are frequently flustered and worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: The foamy bubbles made by soap and water are exactly what a lather consists of.

clue.text: He continues to work for southern transport

parts.note: a cab is a means of transport, a taxi

explanation.surface: A man keeps working to provide transport in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: A scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike-breaker carries on with the job while colleagues walk out.

clue.text: An opening possibly lost

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement of the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A chance that may have been missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of 'lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a narrow aperture, such as one for coins.

clue.text: A romantic tangle

parts.note: suggests a messy love affair, but means a decorative interlaced knot symbolising affection

explanation.surface: A complicated love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A love knot is an ornamental intertwined bow or knot given as a token of devotion.

clue.text: Broken boot-tree found in the garden

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A shoe stretcher, snapped, is discovered out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges the letters of 'boot-tree' (the hyphen is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a vegetable grown in vegetable plots, so something found in a garden.

clue.text: Declined to take a girl back

indicators.note: back means taken backwards, so the girl's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Delia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone refused to give a girl a lift home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DELIA round; 'to take a' is link material. 'Declined' looks like refused, but here means grew weaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ailed is to have been unwell, so to have weakened in health.
